text:
sre-bot: ALERT: API p99 latency spike on prod (global) — +4x vs baseline, starting 1998882200. routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Suspected correlated with last night's CUDA driver + kernel package rollout. metric links: https://metrics.redwood/alerts/INC-3421 :rotating_light:

miguel-sre: seeing the same in Grafana — p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~520ms, p99 to ~1.8s. spike aligns with kernel 5.15.0-115 rollout between 02:10-02:30 UTC on cluster-gpu-3.

karen-cs: multiple enterprise customers just escalated. they see timeouts on long-seq generations, some hit 504s. one customer (ACME) provided repro: 16k token request, concurrency 12, observed staging.

ryan-eng: can we confirm driver version? I see nvidia-driver 525.85.05 deployed to the fleet this morning, previously 515.76. Also CUDA runtime 11.8 -> 12.1 bumped in the image.

nisha-ml: models affected: all 70B transformer variants where KV cache hit rate is high. shorter chat routes less impacted. suspect host-level NVMe IO amplification when many GPUs page memory, plus new driver scheduling interaction.

miguel-sre: checked host dmesg on an affected node: repeated nvme timeouts and block device latencies spiking to 200-400ms under load. iostat shows avg await jumping with queue depth rising. attaching snippet:

```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         1200.0  0.0   51200  0.0   320.0  0.50  96.0
nvme1n1         1100.0  0.0   48000  0.0   290.0  0.45  92.3
```

miguel-sre: also saw kernel stack traces showing blk-mq latencies and driver retry logs referencing firmware timeouts.

liam-infra: we landed blk-mq changes in the image to enable multiqueue, might be interacting badly with the new driver. Also recently switched scheduler to mq-deadline.

ryan-eng: quick mitigation proposal: 1) route high-latency-sensitive traffic to dedicated cluster nodes that we haven't upgraded, 2) reduce max_batch_size on the model server to reduce IO bursts, 3) throttle concurrent long-seq jobs via API rate-limiter, 4) roll back driver on a small canary node to validate.

miguel-sre: doing 1 and 2 now — re-routing 15% traffic to cluster-gpu-1 (pre-upgrade). reducing max_batch_size from 32 -> 8 for affected routes.

ops-bot: deploy to cluster-gpu-1 completed (1998882350).

miguel-sre: preliminary: p95 on canary cluster back to ~140ms after routing change + batch size reduction. global p99 fell to ~950ms but still above baseline.

nisha-ml: suggest also bumping prefix-KV cache TTL and enabling more aggressive prefix caching for long contexts to avoid re-reading KV pages from NVMe during attention recompute.

ryan-eng: creating rollback playbook for driver: plan A = rollback to 515.76 image and restart inferencenodes; Plan B = change scheduler to bfq on affected hosts + increase io-queue-depth tuning. We need to pick one to test on canary tonight.

karen-cs: customers asking for ETA. any chance we can get a temporary SLA credit + status note? I can send interim message if we have a mitigation timeline.

miguel-sre: ETA: will stabilize p95/p99 within 3 hours with routing + batch tweaks. full fleet rollback (if needed) will take 4-6 hours after approval. tagging eng leads.

ryan-eng: I will test rollback on 2 nodes now. commands:
```
sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-515=515.76-ubuntu1
sudo systemctl restart redwood-inferencenode
```

liam-infra: FYI we also have outstanding NVMe firmware 2.0.1 -> 2.0.3 that we postponed; that might be a longer-term fix if vendor confirms bug. I've opened ticket HW-8793 with cloud provider.

miguel-sre: rollbacks started on canary set (nodes: gpu-1-canary-a, gpu-1-canary-b) at 1998882455.

ops-bot: rollback job success on gpu-1-canary-a,b (1998882480).

miguel-sre: after rollback, canary p95 ~130ms, p99 ~210ms. disk await stable <10ms. This points strongly at driver/kernel interaction.

nisha-ml: confirm models on canary show no generation failures. verified ACME repro endpoint returned expected payload.

karen-cs: sending customer update: "We identified a recent GPU driver/kernel combo as the likely cause of increased tail latency. We have mitigations in place and are rolling back on a canary subset; full remediation underway. Will update in 90m." :thumbsup:

ryan-eng: next steps: - schedule full rollback for the rest of the fleet in rolling waves (change window 02:00-08:00 UTC) - engage vendor about firmware + driver interaction - add integration test that runs heavy long-seq generation post-driver-upgrade in staging - create postmortem documenting root cause and runbook (INC-3421).

miguel-sre: creating follow-up tickets: ENG-INFRA-2042 (driver rollback playbook + automation), ENG-RUNTIME-1987 (batching heuristics + safety caps), CS-1120 (customer comms log).

liam-infra: I'll prepare cloud provider escalation and request NVMe firmware advisory.

ryan-eng: action owners: miguel -> coordinate rollback and monitoring, liam -> provider escalation and firmware, nisha -> run model verification and add regression test, karen -> customer comms, I'll own postmortem.

miguel-sre: closing loop: after routing + canary rollback we saw p99 reduced ~4x improvement vs peak and customer reports reduced errors. marking incident as mitigated but still monitoring. scheduling follow-up at 1998886000 for postmortem sync. :white_check_mark:

karen-cs: thanks team. I'll keep CS updated and let account teams know next steps.

ryan-eng: logging final notes: probable root cause = interaction between nvidia-driver 525.x + kernel mq-deadline multiqueue causing NVMe retries under high concurrent KV cache IO; rollback validated hypothesis. Permanent fix = vendor firmware/driver patch or conservative kernel/scheduler settings + improved rollout tests.

miguel-sre: adding runbook excerpt to ENG-SOPs after postmortem: quick checks (iostat, nvme logs, dmesg grep for nvme_errors), temporary mitigations (route, reduce max_batch_size, rollback driver), escalation path to cloud vendor.

ops-bot: Incident INC-3421 marked mitigated at 1998882605.

karen-cs: customers updated. will follow up once postmortem is shared. :pray:
